Three linked, practical courses for biologists who want to analyse their own data — built around real pathogen-genomics and biology examples, with worked exercises and full solutions.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 🐍 [Python for Bioinformatics](python-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
From first principles to packaged, command-line tools and reproducible pipelines.

**4 parts** — foundations, real programming, the ecosystem (NumPy/pandas/Biopython), and your own tools & pipelines (CLI, packaging, subprocess, pysam, Snakemake).

[Start the Python course →](python-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 🧬 [R for Bioinformatics](r-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
From "I can open RStudio" to documented, tested, installable tools.

**5 parts** — the R mindset, files & objects, the tidyverse, Bioconductor, and writing your own package.

[Start the R course →](r-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 📊 [Statistics for Biologists](statistics-for-biologists/index.qmd)
From study design to generalised and mixed models — correctly and reproducibly.

**6 parts** — description, probability, hypothesis testing, linear models, GLMs & mixed models, multivariate methods.

[Start the Stats course →](statistics-for-biologists/index.qmd) · [Which test?](statistics-for-biologists/choosing-a-test.qmd)
:::

:::

## How to use these courses

Each part has **theory** pages and a **code / exercises** page (with downloadable scripts or notebooks and full solutions). Work the theory and exercises together, in order; open the solutions only after trying.

The Python and R courses are companions — the Statistics course assumes the basic R taught in the R course. All example data is in the `downloads/` and `data/` folders of the [repository](https://github.com/USERNAME/bio-courses) — replace `USERNAME` with your GitHub account.
